Easter Island's statues walked. 🗿 Here's how, in 24 seconds. ⏱️

The moai were carved from volcanic stone at Rano Raraku, then moved across the island to platforms on the coast, with no cranes. Researchers think they were "walked": one rope behind to stop it falling forward and two at the sides, pulled left, then right, so the statue rocks and shuffles ahead. Their wide D-shaped bases and forward lean make it work, and the old roads have a curved surface that helps keep them upright.

In a 2012 test, 18 people walked a 4.35-ton replica 100 m in about 40 minutes.

yt_description:
Nearly 1,000 moai were carved at Rano Raraku, an extinct volcano on Rapa Nui. Lipo & Hunt's "walking moai" research: road moai have wide D-shaped bases and lean forward 5–15°, so with one rope behind and two at the sides pulled alternately they rock and shuffle forward along concave roads ~4.5 m wide. In 2012, 18 people walked a 4.35-ton replica 100 m in about 40 minutes.

Sources: https://www.binghamton.edu/news/story/5830/easter-islands-statues-actually-walked-and-physics-backs-it-up · https://www.livescience.com/24312-easter-island-statues-walked.html
Figures are estimates. Stylised 3D animation.
